context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a cloud-hosted SaaS solution that enables public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency while maintaining high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
- Library Management System (Core Cloud-hosted SaaS)
- Payment Gateway (Stripe/Adyen)
- Notification Service (SendGrid/Twilio)
- National Library Registry (EU-hosted REST API)
- Identity Provider (OAuth2/OIDC)

## Relationships
- Patrons and Staff -> Library Management System via HTTPS (UI interaction)
- Library Management System -> Payment Gateway via HTTPS (fine processing)
- Library Management System -> Notification Service via HTTPS (alerts)
- Library Management System -> National Library Registry via HTTPS/REST (metadata synchronization)
- Library Management System -> Identity Provider via OIDC (authentication)

## Technology Stack
- Cloud-hosted SaaS: Core platform architecture
- HTTPS/REST: Secure data transmission and external API integration protocols
- OAuth2/OIDC: Standardized single sign-on authentication for patrons and staff
- Stripe/Adyen & SendGrid/Twilio: Third-party financial and messaging services pinned to EU-region endpoints

## Rationale
This architecture meets all functional requirements for cataloguing and circulation while strictly adhering to EU data residency mandates through regional service pinning. The decoupled external integrations ensure high performance and secure authentication.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It is architected to strictly enforce EU data residency and sub-800ms search performance.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
* Web Application (React/TypeScript SPA)
* API Gateway (Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway)
* Core Domain Service (Java/Spring Boot)
* Search Service (Java with Elasticsearch)
* Notification Worker (Node.js)
* Database (PostgreSQL)
* Message Broker (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka)
* External Systems: Payment Gateway, Notification Service, National Library Registry, Identity Provider

## Relationships
* Web Application calls API Gateway via HTTPS/REST
* API Gateway routes to Core Domain Service and Search Service via gRPC/REST over internal Docker networks
* Core Domain Service reads/writes to PostgreSQL via JDBC over TLS
* Core Domain Service publishes domain events to Message Broker via AMQP
* Notification Worker consumes events from Message Broker via AMQP and calls external Notification Service via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* React/TypeScript: Powers the user-facing Single Page Application via CDN
* Java/Spring Boot: Implements reliable business logic for the Core Domain Service
* Elasticsearch: Powers high-performance catalog searches
* PostgreSQL: Stores relational data, pinned strictly to an EU region for compliance
* RabbitMQ/Apache Kafka: Handles asynchronous event-driven messaging via AMQP
* Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway: Manages edge routing, TLS termination, and rate limiting

## Rationale
Isolating the Elasticsearch-backed Search Service guarantees the strict <800ms search performance requirement without degrading transactional database performance. Pinning PostgreSQL to an EU region strictly satisfies the mandatory EU-only data residency constraint.

Web Application.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency and meets high-performance search requirements.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
* Web Application (React/TypeScript SPA)
* Auth Controller (TypeScript / OIDC Client Library)
* Catalog UI Module (React Components / TanStack Query)
* Circulation Module (React Components)
* API Client (Axios / Fetch API)
* State Management Store (Zustand / Redux Toolkit)
* Router Component (React Router)
* API Gateway (Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway)
* Core Domain Service (Java/Spring Boot)
* Search Service (Java with Elasticsearch)
* Notification Worker (Node.js)
* Database (PostgreSQL)
* Message Broker (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka)
* External Systems: Payment Gateway, Notification Service, National Library Registry, Identity Provider

## Relationships
* Library Patrons and Library Staff -> Web Application: Interacts via [HTTPS]
* Web Application -> API Gateway: Calls APIs via [HTTPS/REST]
* Router Component -> Catalog UI Module & Circulation Module: Lazy-loads views [In-process]
* Auth Controller & UI Modules -> State Management Store: Manages state [In-process]
* Auth Controller & Catalog UI Module -> API Client: Invokes requests [In-process]
* API Client -> API Gateway: Forwards authenticated requests [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
* React/TypeScript SPA: Powers the user-facing Single Page Application via CDN
* Zustand / Redux Toolkit: Manages local application state and caching
* React Router: Handles client-side navigation and lazy-loading
* Java / Spring Boot: Powers core domain services
* Elasticsearch: Ensures 99th-percentile search response under 800 ms
* PostgreSQL: Stores relational data within EU residency constraints

## Rationale
This architecture decouples domain UI modules within a high-performance React SPA while leveraging robust backend services. It strictly enforces EU data residency and optimizes search performance.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures EU-only data residency and meets strict performance constraints like 99th-percentile search responses under 800 ms.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
- Web Application (React/TypeScript SPA)
- API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway container)
- Core Domain Service (Java/Spring Boot)
- Search Service (Java with Elasticsearch)
- Identity Provider, Payment Gateway, Notification Service, National Library Registry (External Systems)
- API Gateway Components: Routing & Load Balancing Component, JWT Validation Filter, Rate Limiting & Throttling Component, Circuit Breaker Component

## Relationships
- Web Application -> API Gateway: Authenticates and routes calls [HTTPS/REST/WebSocket]
- API Gateway -> Identity Provider: Validates tokens [HTTPS/REST]
- Routing Filter -> Core Domain Service: Routes validated commands/queries [gRPC]
- Circuit Breaker -> Search Service: Protects search endpoints [gRPC]

## Technology Stack
- Spring Cloud Gateway: Selected for native reactive routing, dynamic service discovery, and Java ecosystem alignment
- Elasticsearch: Powers fast catalog searches to achieve the <800ms latency requirement
- Resilience4j: Integrated for circuit breaking to prevent cascading failures
- WebClient: Used for non-blocking reactive key caching during JWT validation

## Rationale
This architecture uses reactive, non-blocking routing and caching to minimize latency, satisfying the high-performance search constraint. Spring Cloud Gateway and integrated resilience patterns secure the edge while supporting EU-only data residency.

Core Domain Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Core Domain Service is a Java/Spring Boot container that implements reliable business logic for cataloging and circulation within the Library Management System. It enforces clear bounded contexts while ensuring EU-only data residency and high performance.

## Key Elements
* **Catalog Management Component**: Spring MVC/Data component handling physical and digital items.
* **Circulation & Fines Component**: Manages loans, returns, and payment processing.
* **Event Publisher Component**: Spring AMQP component dispatching domain events.
* **Registry Integration Component**: Spring Cloud OpenFeign component synchronizing metadata.
* **Security Context & Auth Component**: Spring Security component validating tokens locally.

## Relationships
* **API Gateway -> Core Domain Service**: Routes client requests via gRPC and REST.
* **Core Domain Service -> PostgreSQL Database**: Reads and writes relational data using JDBC over TLS.
* **Core Domain Service -> RabbitMQ/Apache Kafka Message Broker**: Publishes domain events via AMQP.
* **Core Domain Service -> Payment Gateway**: Processes library fines via HTTPS.
* **Core Domain Service -> National Library Registry**: Synchronizes metadata via HTTPS/REST.
* **Core Domain Service -> Identity Provider**: Authenticates users using OIDC.

## Technology Stack
* **Java / Spring Boot**: Foundation for robust business logic execution.
* **Spring Modulith**: Enforces package-level boundaries between internal components.
* **Spring Security / OIDC**: Validates JWT tokens locally to minimize latency.
* **Spring Cloud OpenFeign**: Facilitates reliable inter-service REST communication.
* **Spring AMQP**: Handles asynchronous event publishing to message brokers.

## Rationale
Decomposing the container with Spring Modulith isolates domain logic and prevents circular dependencies while maintaining strict EU data boundaries in PostgreSQL. Local JWT validation via Spring Security ensures search and transaction responses remain fast to meet performance constraints.

Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Search Service is a high-performance component of the Library Management System that provides fast catalog searches for library patrons and staff. It is designed to meet strict performance and EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
- API Gateway (Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Search Service (Java with Elasticsearch container)
- API Controller (Spring MVC / Spring WebFlux)
- Query Sanitizer Component (In-memory Java)
- Search Orchestrator (Java Service Bean)
- Elasticsearch Repository (Spring Data Elasticsearch)
- Catalogue Sync Listener (Spring AMQP / Kafka Listener)
- Message Broker (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka)

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> API Controller: Routes search requests [gRPC/REST]
- API Controller -> Query Sanitizer Component: Sanitizes inputs [In-memory Java Method Call]
- Query Sanitizer Component -> Search Orchestrator: Passes clean queries [In-memory Java Method Call]
- Search Orchestrator -> Elasticsearch Repository: Executes queries [Elasticsearch Java Client]
- Message Broker -> Catalogue Sync Listener: Consumes item events [AMQP/Kafka]

## Technology Stack
- Java / Spring Boot: Core component framework
- Elasticsearch: High-performance indexing and search engine
- Spring Data Elasticsearch: Repository data access layer
- Spring MVC / Spring WebFlux: Endpoint exposure
- Spring AMQP / Kafka Listener: Event ingestion

## Rationale
This architecture decouples ingestion from query paths to maintain high performance and meet the sub-800ms search latency requirement. It also integrates sanitization to ensure compliance with EU data residency rules.

Notification Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Notification Worker is an event-driven component of the Library Management System that reliably processes asynchronous events to deliver notifications to patrons and staff. It ensures system resilience through local rate-limiting, retry logic, and strict adherence to EU data residency constraints.

## Key Elements
- Message Consumer (Node.js/amqplib)
- Notification Router (TypeScript)
- Delivery Client (Axios)
- Retry Coordinator (TypeScript/Bottleneck)
- Dead Letter Handler
- Message Broker (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka)
- External Notification Service

## Relationships
- Message Consumer -> Message Broker: Consumes events [AMQP]
- Message Consumer -> Notification Router: Passes deserialized events [In-memory function call]
- Notification Router -> Delivery Client: Sends formatted payload [In-memory function call]
- Delivery Client -> Retry Coordinator: Forwards failed requests [In-memory function call]
- Delivery Client -> Notification Service: Sends notifications [HTTPS]
- Retry Coordinator -> Notification Service: Retries requests [HTTPS]
- Dead Letter Handler -> Message Broker: Routes poison messages to DLQ [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js: Provides fast asynchronous I/O and low memory overhead for event-driven processing.
- TypeScript: Ensures type safety across the worker's internal routing and retry logic.
- amqplib: Enables reliable message consumption over the AMQP protocol.
- Axios: Handles outbound, timeout-managed HTTPS requests to the external provider.
- Bottleneck: Manages exponential backoff and rate limiting locally for transient failure handling.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures high reliability and fault tolerance when communicating with external third-party systems. Localizing retry state and rate-limiting within the EU boundary satisfies strict data residency mandates while meeting system resilience goals.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive digital solution for public and academic libraries designed to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals. It enforces strict EU-only data residency while maintaining high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
*   Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
*   Web Application (React/TypeScript SPA)
*   API Gateway (Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway)
*   Core Domain Service (Java/Spring Boot)
*   Search Service (Java with Elasticsearch)
*   Notification Worker (Node.js)
*   Database Container: Primary PostgreSQL Instance, PostgreSQL Read Replicas, PgBouncer Connection Pooler, Audit Logging Subsystem (`pgAudit`), and `pg_trgm` Extension
*   Message Broker (RabbitMQ / Apache Kafka)
*   External Systems: Payment Gateway, Notification Service, National Library Registry, Identity Provider

## Relationships
*   `Core Domain Service -> PgBouncer`: Acquires database connections [TCP/IP over TLS]
*   `Search Service -> PgBouncer`: Reads catalogue delta for indexing [TCP/IP over TLS]
*   `PgBouncer -> Primary PostgreSQL / Read Replicas`: Routes queries [PostgreSQL Native Protocol over TLS]

## Technology Stack
*   **PostgreSQL**: Selected for robust relational OLTP data management and strict compliance with EU-only data residency constraints.
*   **PgBouncer**: Deployed for efficient database connection pooling under high concurrency.
*   **pg_trgm Extension**: Enabled in PostgreSQL to support fast fuzzy-text searches, meeting performance requirements.
*   **pgAudit**: Utilized for native audit logging to ensure strict EU data governance compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures low-latency performance with 99th-percentile search responses under 800 ms through optimized database read replicas and connection pooling. It strictly enforces EU data residency and governance requirements via localized deployment and native auditing tools.

Message Broker.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It utilizes an event-driven architecture to process circulation tasks and maintain EU-only data residency.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons and Library Staff (Users)
- Web Application (React/TypeScript SPA)
- API Gateway (Nginx / Spring Cloud Gateway)
- Core Domain Service (Java/Spring Boot)
- Search Service (Java with Elasticsearch)
- Notification Worker (Node.js)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Message Broker (RabbitMQ) containing Exchange Component, notification-queue, audit-event-queue, and Data Policy Enforcement Component
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, Notification Service, National Library Registry, Identity Provider

## Relationships
- Library Patrons / Staff -> Web Application [HTTPS]
- Web Application -> API Gateway [HTTPS/JSON]
- API Gateway -> Core Domain Service & Search Service [gRPC/HTTP]
- Core Domain Service -> Message Broker (Exchange Component) [AMQP]
- Exchange Component -> notification-queue & audit-event-queue [AMQP]
- notification-queue -> Notification Worker [AMQP]
- Message Broker -> Local Storage Volume [File I/O]

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: Powers the frontend SPA for high responsiveness.
- Java/Spring Boot: Implements the robust Core Domain Service.
- Elasticsearch: Delivers sub-800ms 99th-percentile search performance.
- RabbitMQ: Handles asynchronous event-driven messaging via AMQP.
- PostgreSQL: Provides reliable relational persistence.

## Rationale
This architecture meets performance requirements through dedicated Elasticsearch indexing while ensuring strict EU data residency compliance via local RabbitMQ storage policies.
